title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space and defense sectors are grappling with challenges ranging from missile production bottlenecks to the complexities of satellite network resilience. Meanwhile, the commercial space race continues to heat up, with significant funding rounds and strategic partnerships making headlines.

themes.title: Satellite Network Resilience
themes.body: DARPA's new initiative to explore rapid satellite network reconstruction highlights the growing concern over vulnerabilities in space infrastructure. As geopolitical tensions rise, the ability to quickly restore capabilities will be crucial for national security.

themes.title: Funding and Partnerships
themes.body: True Anomaly's recent $190M Series C round underscores the increasing investor interest in space tech, while Anduril and L3Harris's tactical constellation bid signals a shift towards collaborative defense strategies. Expect more alliances as companies seek to navigate a competitive landscape.

themes.title: Missile Production Challenges
themes.body: The ongoing solid rocket motor bottleneck is a stark reminder of the fragility in defense supply chains, potentially delaying critical missile production. As budgets swell, the industry must address these production hurdles to meet rising demands.

themes.title: Commercial Space Developments
themes.body: The buzz around SpaceX's trading debut and the implications for Elon Musk's wealth are hard to ignore, but the real story lies in the broader commercial landscape. With companies like Viasat and Calian securing government contracts, the private sector's role in national defense is becoming more pronounced.
